text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malaysia wants South Korea to take measures to correct the trade imbalance between the two countries which currently is in favour of the latter.
- Taxi rides will cost more from December 15 with passengers having to pay extra if they are caught in traffic jams. Taxi drivers will have to wear uniforms.
- Construction work on the 13.6 billion ringgit Bakun Hydroelectric project will start on December 1, a month ahead of schedule, and is expected to be completed in five years.
- Four of the five major concerns cited by Japanese investors about investing in Malaysia are related to labour.

- The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and the Korea Stock Exchange have signed a memorandum of understanding which is aimed at providing a mechanism for developing long-term cooperation and channels of communications between the two exchanges.
- Education Minister Najib Tun Razak has blamed parents for pressuring pupils to excel in examinations.
